1. Load data, fix time, remove lanes that don't have samples, and combine data (i.e., plate 2 is X time later after the latest reading of plate 1)
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

OD600 <- read_excel("~/GitHub/VirosporeQuant/SPO1_mutant/Data/20261002_mutant_virulence_curves_plate1.xlsx", sheet = "OD600_1")
OD600_2 <- read_excel("~/GitHub/VirosporeQuant/SPO1_mutant/Data/20261002_mutant_virulence_curves_plate2.xlsx", sheet = "OD600_2")
```

2. Fix time column in data
```{r}
# Fix time so that it's represented as a decimal
OD600 <- OD600 %>%
  mutate(Time = hour(Time) + minute(Time)/60 + second(Time)/3600)
OD600_2 <- OD600_2 %>%
  mutate(Time = hour(Time) + minute(Time)/60 + second(Time)/3600)
# Fix the time over 24 hrs in OD600_2
  OD600_2 <- OD600_2 %>%
  mutate(
    Time = Time + cumsum(c(FALSE, diff(Time) < 0)) * 24
  )
# Shift data2 time and Combine data
last.time <- max(OD600$Time, na.rm = TRUE)
OD600_2 <- OD600_2 %>%
  mutate(Time = Time + last.time)
# Combine both OD600 tables (the reason there are 2 tables is because the experiment is stopped and re-started once phage is added)
OD600_full <- bind_rows(OD600, OD600_2)
# Remove temperature from data
OD600_full <- OD600_full %>%
  select(-Temp)
# Remove lanes and wells that don't have samples 
OD600_full <- OD600_full %>%
  select(
    -c(E1, F1, G1, H1),
    -matches("(9|10|11|12)$")
  )

```

3. Reshape data for initial plotting
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

OD600_long <- OD600_full %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Time,
    names_to = "Well",
    values_to = "OD600"
  )

# Extract plate column number and assign treatments
OD600_long <- OD600_long %>%
  mutate(
    Column = as.numeric(gsub("[A-H]", "", Well))
  )

OD600_long <- OD600_long %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = case_when(
      Column == 1 ~ "DSM control",
      Column == 2 ~ "Control no phage",
      Column == 3 ~ "Mutant MOI 0.1",
      Column == 4 ~ "Mutant MOI 1",
      Column == 5 ~ "Mutant MOI 10",
      Column == 6 ~ "Wildtype MOI 0.1",
      Column == 7 ~ "Wildtype MOI 1",
      Column == 8 ~ "Wildtype MOI 10"
    )
  )

# Also add the genotype data separately
OD600_long <- OD600_long %>%
  mutate(
    Genotype = case_when(
      Column %in% 3:5 ~ "mutant",
      Column %in% 6:8 ~ "wildtype",
      TRUE ~ "control"
    ),
    
    MOI = case_when(
      Column %in% c(3, 6) ~ 0.1,
      Column %in% c(4, 7) ~ 1,
      Column %in% c(5, 8) ~ 10,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )
# Add replicate information as well 

OD600_long <- OD600_long %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  mutate(
    Replicate = as.integer(factor(Well))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

########## DATA TRUNCATION ###############
APPROACH 1:
- Drop control from dataset
- Truncate the data for each replicate for each genotype based on global min following first global max
- Calculate AUC (biomass loss)--this is not virulence
- Correct for population specific adjustments

```{r}
OD600_long_nocontrol <- OD_data_corrected %>%
  filter(Treatment != "Control no phage",
         Treatment != "DSM control")
```

```{r}
 #Function to identify first minimum after first maximum
truncate_curve <- function(od) {

  d <- diff(od)

  if (length(d) == 0) {
    return(seq_along(od))
  }

  # First maximum: OD600 starts decreasing
  max_idx <- which(d < 0)[1]

  if (is.na(max_idx)) {
    return(seq_along(od))
  }

  # First minimum after maximum
  after_max <- d[max_idx:length(d)]
  stop_idx <- which(after_max >= 0)[1]

  if (is.na(stop_idx)) {
    min_idx <- length(od)
  } else {
    min_idx <- max_idx + stop_idx - 1
  }

  seq_len(min_idx)
}

# 1. Truncate data (no controls included)
truncated_infected_min_app1 <- OD600_long_nocontrol %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Genotype, MOI, Replicate, Well) %>%
  arrange(Time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  group_modify(~ .x[truncate_curve(.x$OD600_corrected), ]) %>%
  ungroup()

# Plot to double check that the correct thing was done 
ggplot(
  truncated_infected_min_app1,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = OD600_corrected,
    group = Well,
    color = Treatment
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = expression(OD[600])
  ) 


```

7. Calculate AUC for each genotype (so this is not actually virulence just a measure of biomass)
```{r}
library(DescTools)
library(dplyr)

library(dplyr)
library(DescTools)


infection_time <- 4.73

auc_data_trunc_min_app1 <- truncated_infected_min_app1 %>%
  filter(
    Time >= infection_time,
    Genotype %in% c("mutant", "wildtype")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Well, Treatment, Genotype, MOI, Replicate) %>%
  arrange(Time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(
    AUC = if (n() >= 2) {
      DescTools::AUC(
        x = Time,
        y = OD600_corrected,
        method = "trapezoid"
      )
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    start_time = min(Time),
    end_time = max(Time),
    duration = end_time - start_time,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

auc_data_trunc_min_app1

# Account for different truncation times between replicates
auc_data_trunc_min_app1_normalized <- auc_data_trunc_min_app1 %>%
  mutate(
    mean_OD600 = AUC / duration
  )

# Plot to compare mutant and wildtpye (RAW)

library(ggplot2)

auc.fig_app1_raw <- ggplot(
  auc_data_trunc_min_app1,
  aes(
    x = factor(MOI),
    y = AUC,
    fill = Genotype
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.6,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = Genotype),
    position = position_jitterdodge(
      jitter.width = 0.1,
      dodge.width = 0.8
    ),
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "wildtype" = "#638B66FF",
      "mutant" = "#A2CEAAFF"
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "wildtype" = "#638B66FF",
      "mutant" = "#A2CEAAFF"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Multiplicity of infection (MOI)",
    y = expression(AUC~(OD[600] %.% h))
  )

auc.fig_app1_raw
```

############## APPROACH 2 #####################
- Use blank corrected dataset and remove the DSM blanks from that dataset (keep non infected control so that we can calculate virulence)
- Calculate virulence between genotypes relative to the control 
- Correct for population specific adjustments 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(DescTools)

infection_time <- 4.73

# 1. Mean blank-corrected control curve
control_curve <- OD_data_corrected %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Control no phage") %>%
  group_by(Time) %>%
  summarise(
    control_OD600 = mean(OD600_corrected, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Time)

# 2. Calculate infected and time-matched control AUC
auc_data_trunc_min.app2 <- truncated_infected_min_app1 %>%
  filter(
    Time >= infection_time,
    Genotype %in% c("mutant", "wildtype")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Well, Treatment, Genotype, MOI, Replicate) %>%
  arrange(Time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    df <- .x

    if (nrow(df) < 2) {
      return(tibble(
        AUC = NA_real_,
        control_AUC = NA_real_,
        duration = NA_real_,
        Virulence = NA_real_
      ))
    }

    # Infected AUC
    infected_auc <- DescTools::AUC(
      x = df$Time,
      y = df$OD600_corrected,
      method = "trapezoid"
    )

    # Control OD600 at the same timepoints
    matched_control <- approx(
      x = control_curve$Time,
      y = control_curve$control_OD600,
      xout = df$Time,
      rule = 1
    )$y

    control_auc <- if (all(is.finite(matched_control))) {
      DescTools::AUC(
        x = df$Time,
        y = matched_control,
        method = "trapezoid"
      )
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }

    # Duration-corrected relative virulence
    virulence <- if (
      is.finite(control_auc) && control_auc > 0
    ) {
      1 - infected_auc / control_auc
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }

    tibble(
      AUC = infected_auc,
      control_AUC = control_auc,
      duration = max(df$Time) - min(df$Time),
      Virulence = virulence
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Final dataset
virulence_data_trunc_min.app2 <- auc_data_trunc_min.app2



# Plot 
virulence_data_trunc_min.app2 <- virulence_data_trunc_min.app2 %>%
  mutate(
    MOI_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(MOI))
  )

virulence.reg_trunc_app2_plot <- ggplot(
  virulence_data_trunc_min.app2,
  aes(
    x = MOI_numeric,
    y = Virulence,
    color = Genotype,
    fill = Genotype
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.7,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.03)
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
  values = c(
    "mutant" = "#D55E00",
    "wildtype" = "#0072B2"
  )
) +
scale_fill_manual(
  values = c(
    "mutant" = "red",
    "wildtype" = "blue"
  )) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "MOI",
    y = "Relative virulence",
    color = "Phage genotype",
    fill = "Phage genotype"
  ) 

virulence.reg_trunc_app2_plot
```
# Some takeaways: 
The data is super sensitive to how its analyzed, which is not a good sign
We need to think about the time of infection here with respect to Spo0A onset. Our original hypothesis is that the mutant will be more virulent in the prescence of Spo0A (because no functioning 0A boxes = no lytic shut down). In previous experiments (with the old mutant prior to 2026), I added in the Spo0A gfp strain to the experiment as a marker for when sporulation started. I need to do that again when I run this experiment again and perhaps alter the time of infection based on that. Considering this, it might be the case that we have not captured virulence measurements at the right time with respect to sporulation.

##### TRUNCATING BY TIME AND NOT BY POPULATION MINS ##########
We need to probably truncate the OD600 values after each minimum is reached for each treatment, I assume this would be at the replicate level (i.e., find the minimum od600 for each well and then cut when it reaches the min )
```{r}
# Truncate the data when the minimum value is reached
library(dplyr)


# Function to identify first minimum after first maximum
truncate_curve <- function(od) {

  d <- diff(od)

  if (length(d) == 0) {
    return(seq_along(od))
  }

  # First maximum: OD600 starts decreasing
  max_idx <- which(d < 0)[1]

  if (is.na(max_idx)) {
    return(seq_along(od))
  }

  # First minimum after maximum
  after_max <- d[max_idx:length(d)]
  stop_idx <- which(after_max >= 0)[1]

  if (is.na(stop_idx)) {
    min_idx <- length(od)
  } else {
    min_idx <- max_idx + stop_idx - 1
  }

  seq_len(min_idx)
}

# 1. Truncate infected replicates only
truncated_infected_min <- OD600_long %>%
  filter(
    Treatment != "Control no phage",
    Treatment != "DSM control"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Genotype, MOI, Replicate, Well) %>%
  arrange(Time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  group_modify(~ .x[truncate_curve(.x$OD600), ]) %>%
  ungroup()

# 2. Calculate average truncation time for each treatment
mean_truncation_times <- truncated_infected_min%>%
  group_by(Treatment, Genotype, MOI, Replicate, Well) %>%
  summarise(
    truncation_time = max(Time),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Genotype, MOI) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_truncation_time = mean(truncation_time),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Keep original no-phage control
control_data <- OD600_long %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Control no phage")

# 4. Create treatment-specific truncated controls
control_truncated <- tidyr::crossing(
  control_data,
  mean_truncation_times %>%
    rename(
      Reference_Treatment = Treatment,
      Reference_Genotype = Genotype,
      Reference_MOI = MOI
    )
) %>%
  filter(Time <= mean_truncation_time)

# 5. Combine infected and control data
truncated_data_min <- bind_rows(
  truncated_infected_min,
  control_truncated
)


# Plot to double check that the correct thing was done 
ggplot(
  truncated_data_min,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = OD600,
    group = Well,
    color = Treatment
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = expression(OD[600])
  ) 
mean_truncation_times  
```

##### INITIAL TRUNCATION APPROACH; TRUNCATING BY TIME AND NOT BY POPULATION MINS ########
Initial truncation --truncating all samples at 7 h
After taking a second look at the data, there is the rise of mutants at about hour 10, and because we don't want this to influence our virulence measurements, we need to truncate the data 
Let's truncate the data at 8 hours and then replot to see what we are working with

3. Calculate virulence 
```{r}
library(DescTools)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
# Filter data based on time of infection time of infection = 4.73 so filter all data after that to calculate AUC
virulence.od_trunc_MIN <- truncated_data_min %>%
  filter(Time >= 4.73)

auc_data_trunc_min <- virulence.od_trunc_MIN %>%
  group_by(Well, Treatment, Genotype, MOI) %>%
  summarise(
    AUC = AUC(
      x = Time,
      y = OD600,
      method = "trapezoid"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
auc_data_trunc_min

# Calculate control AUC
control_auc_trunc_min <- auc_data_trunc_min %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Control no phage") %>%
  summarise(
    mean_control_AUC = mean(AUC, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pull(mean_control_AUC)

# Calculate virulence
auc_data_trunc_min <- auc_data_trunc_min %>%
  mutate(
    Virulence = 1 - (AUC / control_auc_trunc_min)
  )
# Subset virulence data for mutant and genotype not the control 
virulence_data_trunc_min <- auc_data_trunc_min %>%
  filter(Genotype %in% c("mutant", "wildtype"))
```

```{r}
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = expression(OD[600]),
    color = "Treatment"
  ) 
```


6. Plot individual replicate growth curves
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)


# Add a replicate column 
library(dplyr)

virulence.od_trunc <- virulence.od_trunc %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  mutate(
    Replicate = as.integer(factor(Well))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Prepare data
plot_data <- virulence.od_trunc %>%
  mutate(
    Genotype = case_when(
      grepl("Wildtype", Treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Wildtype",
      grepl("Mutant", Treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Mutant",
      grepl("Control no phage", Treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Control",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    MOI = case_when(
      grepl("MOI 0.1$", Treatment) ~ "0.1",
      grepl("MOI 1$", Treatment) ~ "1",
      grepl("MOI 10$", Treatment) ~ "10",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Genotype))

# Replicate control across all MOI panels
control_data <- plot_data %>%
  filter(Genotype == "Control") %>%
  select(-MOI) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(MOI = c("0.1", "1", "10"))

# Combine treatment and control data
plot_data <- bind_rows(
  plot_data %>% filter(Genotype != "Control"),
  control_data
) %>%
  mutate(
    Genotype = factor(
      Genotype,
      levels = c("Control", "Wildtype", "Mutant")
    ),
    MOI = factor(MOI, levels = c("0.1", "1", "10"))
  )

# Plot individual replicate curves
plot.od <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = OD600,
    color = Genotype,
    linetype = Genotype,
    group = interaction(Genotype, MOI, Replicate)
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.65,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ MOI,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 4.73,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "gray40"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Control" = "black",
      "Wildtype" = "blue",
      "Mutant" = "red"
    )
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Control" = "solid",
      "Wildtype" = "solid",
      "Mutant" = "solid"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = expression(OD[600]),
    color = "Treatment",
    linetype = "Treatment"
  ) 
plot.od

ggsave(
  "moi_panel_1002plate_truncated.png",
  plot = plot.od,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r}
virulence_model <- lm(
  Virulence ~ log10(MOI_numeric) * Genotype,
  data = virulence_data
)

summary(virulence_model)
```

Dissecting the output of the lm
Call:
lm(formula = Virulence ~ log10(MOI_numeric) * Genotype, data = virulence_data)

Residuals:
      Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
-0.184594 -0.032322 -0.002533  0.033233  0.150043 

Coefficients:
                                  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)                        0.12873    0.01331   9.675 1.84e-12 ***
log10(MOI_numeric)                 0.05274    0.01630   3.236  0.00230 ** 
Genotypemutant                    -0.02070    0.01882  -1.100  0.27733    
log10(MOI_numeric):Genotypemutant -0.06851    0.02305  -2.973  0.00477 ** 
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

Residual standard error: 0.06519 on 44 degrees of freedom # root mean squared error, i.e., what is the average error on this dataset i.e., how far away are the points away from the predicted points of the mode, measures the quality of the fit in units of the outcome variable, 

Multiple R-squared:  0.2229,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.1699  # information about the fit of the model, and adjustment for the number of different predictors in the model, the model was only able to predict about 22% 
F-statistic: 4.206 on 3 and 44 DF,  p-value: 0.01061

#
Standard error: a measure how far off we expect the estimates to be based on the values of all of the data (what it really is is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution)

T statistic: the ratio of estimate to std error, can be interpreted as a signal to noise ratio, ie. how big the estimate is relative to the error, t stats that are higher in their value of absolute magnitude  , higher t stats reflect parameters that are more precisely estimated relative to their magnitude 

Probability greater than abs value of t
